subject: ClinicalWrap billing rails, itemized SKU packaging, and PO field constraints
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@clinicalwrap.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clinicalwrap.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Packaging our purchase requirements + PO template (attached)

Hi Maya / Vanessa,

Thanks for the call earlier. Per procurement's checklist I'm sharing our PO template — attached — and a short list of gating items we need clarified before we can issue a blanket PO. High level: we need (1) explicit PO header fields (PO number, remit-to address + remit account, bill-to entity, BU code), (2) confirmation we can receive itemized invoices per PO line (we need one invoice per shipment/line until we reach the monthly threshold), (3) an invoice cadence option where we can opt into weekly statements or a consolidated monthly statement, and (4) the default net terms we should expect.

Two specific packaging questions from the supply side team: ClinicalWrap breaks charges out by SKU pack size and unit-of-measure — they require the vendor invoice to include both the pack-size attribute and the unit price per SKU for downstream reconciliation. Will Redwood be able to provide item-level tax and SKU pack-size metadata on invoices (CSV export preferred)?

Attached: ClinicalWrap_PO_Template.pdf

Goal: if those items are resolvable we can get a blanket PO in the next week and sign a standard commitment.

Jordan Lee
Sr. Procurement Manager
ClinicalWrap

On Tue, Jun 22, 2027 at 07:44 AM Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com> wrote:
> Jordan — appreciate the list. I looped in Vanessa and Finance ops (Karthik) to confirm what we can commit to and how we handle the export schema. Quick answers up front: Redwood can support explicit PO headers, and we can produce CSV invoice exports with line-level SKU attributes. The remaining items are negotiable: invoice cadence and net terms depend on the commercial tier and whether ClinicalWrap wants itemized per-shipment invoices or a consolidated statement.
>
> I'll ask Vanessa to surface the commercial tradeoffs (discounts vs. invoice consolidation) and Karthik to confirm the exact CSV fields we can output from our billing system. If you can share a sample of how your ERP expects the pack-size field rendered (column name / example), that will speed mapping.
>
> Cheers,
> Maya
> Head of Account Management, Redwood Inference
>
>

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan@clinicalwrap.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ClinicalWrap billing rails, itemized SKU packaging, and PO field constraints

Jordan — thanks for the template and the clear list. Follow-up and proposed options from Redwood: 

1) PO headers: we can populate PO number, remit-to, remit account, bill-to entity and a custom "BU / cost center" field. We'll need ClinicalWrap to return the exact field labels you want on the PO so our ingestion can map them one-to-one.

2) Itemized SKU packaging & CSV export: Karthik confirms we can deliver a CSV export per invoice that contains: invoice_id, invoice_date, po_number, line_number, sku, pack_size, unit_of_measure, unit_price, quantity, line_tax, and accounting_code. We'll attach a sample export file (redwood_invoice_sample.csv) for your review. If your ERP wants different column names, send the sample and we'll remap.

3) Invoice cadence: two supported patterns — a) consolidated monthly statement (single invoice per legal entity per month) or b) per-shipment line-item invoices. If you choose per-shipment invoices we can support weekly batching to reduce AP overhead. Note: per-shipment invoices increase our transaction processing cost; we typically require an administrative fee for cohorts requesting weekly statements unless the annual commitment meets the rebate threshold.

4) Net terms: Standard is net30 for enterprise customers on annual commitments. For month-to-month or lower commitments default is net45. Vanessa: can you add the commercial concession matrix (what threshold moves net45 -> net30 and the associated discount impact)?

5) Itemization and PO split behavior: we can support "one invoice per PO line up to X lines" or full consolidation. If ClinicalWrap needs line-level remittance routing (different remit-to by SKU or BU) we need that defined in the PO as separate lines with the remit-to field populated.

Next steps: Vanessa will propose a commercial tradeoff (discount vs invoice cadence). Jordan — if you can return a single sample of the ERP mapping (column names + example row) we'll validate the redwoodInvoice CSV mapping and provide a final mapping doc by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Maya

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan@clinicalwrap.com>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ClinicalWrap billing rails, itemized SKU packaging, and PO field constraints

Jordan — quick commercial note to make the choices explicit:

Option A (lower admin cost to Redwood): Consolidated monthly statement + net30 — requires a 12-month commit at $180k ARR (tier 2). This gives a 7% platform discount and waives the weekly-statement admin fee.

Option B (max flexibility for ClinicalWrap): Weekly itemized invoices per shipment + net45 — no platform discount; administrative fee of $750/month to cover processing weekly invoices.

Option C (hybrid): Monthly consolidated invoices for most SKUs, but we can carve out up to 5 high-variance SKUs for weekly itemized invoices. This requires a 6-month commit at $120k ARR and gives a 3% discount; administrative fee waived for the carved SKUs.

We generally find most procurement teams prefer Option A (single invoice + better unit economics). If ClinicalWrap is open to Option A we can accelerate the PO issuance and drop the deal into the contract queue. If you need net60 we can discuss a short-term credit holdback but that will reduce the discount band.

Maya / Karthik: any constraints on how quickly we can flip the CSV mapping and produce a test file? Jordan — I'll follow up with a redline of the commercial terms and the simple SOW language for the PO that includes the required header fields.

—Vanessa
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@clinicalwrap.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clinicalwrap.com
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ClinicalWrap billing rails, itemized SKU packaging, and PO field constraints

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement prefers Option C as a starting point (we can carve out the five skus that drive the most reconciliation variance). A few clarifications before we proceed: 

• We need the CSV column names to be exactly: po_number, invoice_id, invoice_date, line_number, sku_code, pack_size, uom, unit_price, qty, line_tax, account_code. If Redwood can send the sample mapped exactly that way we can run a quick import test.
• ClinicalWrap can accept net30 if Redwood will add a 45-day holdback clause (5% of each invoice held and released on 45-day reconciliation) OR we accept net45 with the 3% discount in Option C. Our finance director prefers net30 but will consider the net45 + deeper discount path.
• DocuSign: we'll execute the blanket PO once the SOW includes the header fields + carveout list. Sharing DocuSign link to our PO routing: https://www.docusign.com/CLW-PO-0093.

If you can turn around the CSV sample today and the SOW redline, we can route the PO this week.

Jordan
Sr. Procurement Manager, ClinicalWrap
